title: Long sentences
title_target: Om du vill, kan jag skriva en kort text
goal: Build long, well-shaped sentences: put a whole clause in first position, report questions without inverting, and chain *att*, *om* and *när* clauses without losing track of the verb.
bekal: start a sentence with a subordinate clause and keep the verb next (*Om du vill, kan vi…*)
turn direct questions into indirect ones (*Vet du när han kommer?*)
link three or four clauses into one smooth sentence
wave: Go back to Svenska 102, Unit 15 (indirect speech): take five questions you asked someone this week and report them aloud — *Jag frågade om…*, *Jag undrade vad…* — watching that *inte* comes before the verb.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Skisserna
dialogs.intro: Dian has spent two days on sketches for the client in Borås. On Wednesday afternoon Karin stops by her desk with the printouts in her hand.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Hej Dian, har du en minut? Jag har tittat på dina skisser.
lines.id: Hi Dian, have you got a minute? I've looked at your sketches.
lines.literal: hi Dian, have you a minute? I have looked at your sketches.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Ja, absolut. Vad tycker du?
lines.id: Yes, of course. What do you think?
lines.literal: yes, absolutely. what think you?

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Jag tycker att de är snygga, men jag undrar om kunden förstår vad de visar.
lines.id: I think they look good, but I wonder if the client will understand what they show.
lines.literal: I think that they are nice-looking, but I wonder if client-the understands what they show.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Hur menar du? Är de för otydliga?
lines.id: What do you mean? Are they too unclear?
lines.literal: how mean you? are they too unclear?

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Nej, men eftersom kunden aldrig har sett sådana här skisser, behöver vi förklara dem.
lines.id: No, but since the client has never seen sketches like these, we need to explain them.
lines.literal: no, but since client-the never has seen such here sketches, need we explain them.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Om du vill, kan jag skriva en kort text under varje bild.
lines.id: If you like, I can write a short text under each picture.
lines.literal: if you want, can I write a short text under every picture.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Bra idé. Och när du har gjort det, kan du skicka dem till Mattias, så att han hinner kolla dem.
lines.id: Good idea. And when you've done that, you can send them to Mattias, so that he has time to check them.
lines.literal: good idea. and when you have done it, can you send them to Mattias, so that he has-time check them.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Visst. Vet du när han kommer tillbaka från lunchen?
lines.id: Sure. Do you know when he's coming back from lunch?
lines.literal: sure. know you when he comes back from lunch-the?

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Ingen aning, men jag vet att han har ett möte klockan två.
lines.id: No idea, but I know he has a meeting at two o'clock.
lines.literal: no idea, but I know that he has a meeting clock-the two.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Då skickar jag dem innan han går på mötet.
lines.id: Then I'll send them before he goes to the meeting.
lines.literal: then send I them before he goes on meeting-the.

lines.speaker: Karin:
lines.text: Perfekt. Och Dian – det syns att du har jobbat hårt. Bra jobbat!
lines.id: Perfect. And Dian — it shows that you've worked hard. Well done!
lines.literal: perfect. and Dian – it is-seen that you have worked hard. good worked!

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Tack, vad roligt att höra!
lines.id: Thanks, that's lovely to hear!
lines.literal: thanks, what fun to hear!

notes: **Jag undrar om kunden förstår vad de visar** — one sentence, three clauses: a main clause, an *om*-clause (whether), and a *vad*-clause inside that. Each subordinate clause keeps straight word order, subject before verb: *om **kunden förstår***, *vad **de visar***.

**Eftersom kunden aldrig har sett…, behöver vi…** — the whole *eftersom*-clause fills the first slot, so the main clause has to continue with the **verb**: *behöver vi*. Notice *aldrig* before *har*: BIFF applies to every sentence adverb, not just *inte*.

**Sådana här skisser** — "sketches like these". *Sådan* (**SOH-dahn**) means "such, that kind of"; *sådan här* = this kind, *sådan där* = that kind. In speech it shrinks to *sån här* / *sånt här* / *såna här*.

**Så att han hinner kolla dem** — *så att* introduces purpose or result: "so that". Don't mix it up with plain *så* at the start of a main clause ("so, then"), which is followed by the verb: *Så skickade jag dem.*

**Det syns att…** — *synas* (**SÜ-nahs**), "to be visible, to show", is one of the -s verbs from Svenska 102. *Det syns att du har jobbat hårt* = "It shows that you've worked hard". Its sister *det märks att…* means "you can tell that…".
**Bra jobbat!** — "Well done!", literally "good worked". Swedish praise is usually short and low-key, so when your boss says *Bra jobbat!*, take it as a real compliment.

grammars.title: A whole clause in first position
body: The first slot of a main clause (the *fundament*) can hold a single word — *Idag kommer han* — or a whole subordinate clause. The rule doesn't change: whatever fills the first slot, the **finite verb comes next**, then the subject.

head: First slot (subordinate clause)
Verb
Subject
Rest
rows: Eftersom kunden aldrig har sett sådana skisser,

after: The **comma** after the first clause is optional in Swedish, and many writers leave it out in short sentences: *Om du vill kan jag skriva en text.* Use it when the sentence is long — it helps the reader.

In speech, Swedes often add a little **så** before the verb: *Om du vill, **så** kan jag hjälpa dig.* It works like English "then" in "If you want, then I can…". Fine in conversation, but leave it out in formal writing.
The most common mistake is to keep subject-first order in the main clause: *Om du vill, jag kan…* (wrong). Say it aloud a few times: *Om du vill, **kan jag**… När jag kommer hem, **ringer jag**…*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Planer för lördagen
dialogs.intro: On Thursday evening Oskar calls Dian. He has an idea for the weekend: a day out in the Göteborg archipelago, the hundreds of islands just outside the city.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Tjena! Vad gör du på lördag?
lines.id: Hey! What are you doing on Saturday?
lines.literal: hi! what do you on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Jag vet inte än. Varför undrar du?
lines.id: I don't know yet. Why do you ask?
lines.literal: I know not yet. why wonder you?

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Om vädret är fint, tänkte jag att vi kunde åka ut i skärgården.
lines.id: If the weather's nice, I thought we could go out to the archipelago.
lines.literal: if weather-the is nice, thought I that we could go out in archipelago-the.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Gärna! Men jag vet inte hur man tar sig dit.
lines.id: I'd love to! But I don't know how you get there.
lines.literal: gladly! but I know not how one takes oneself there.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Man tar spårvagnen till Saltholmen och sedan båten till Styrsö. Det tar ungefär en timme.
lines.id: You take the tram to Saltholmen and then the boat to Styrsö. It takes about an hour.
lines.literal: one takes tram-the to Saltholmen and then boat-the to Styrsö. it takes about an hour.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Vet du om mitt månadskort gäller på båten också?
lines.id: Do you know if my monthly pass is valid on the boat too?
lines.literal: know you if my month-card applies on boat-the also?

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Ja, det ingår. Kan du kolla när båtarna går? Jag har ingen tidtabell här.
lines.id: Yes, it's included. Can you check when the boats leave? I don't have a timetable here.
lines.literal: yes, it is-included. can you check when boats-the go? I have no timetable here.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Visst. Men vad gör vi om det regnar?
lines.id: Sure. But what do we do if it rains?
lines.literal: sure. but what do we if it rains?

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Om det regnar, går vi på Universeum i stället.
lines.id: If it rains, we'll go to Universeum instead.
lines.literal: if it rains, go we on Universeum in place.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Bra plan. Jag undrar bara om jag hinner hem innan sju, eftersom jag ska ringa mamma då.
lines.id: Good plan. I just wonder if I'll make it home before seven, because I'm calling my mom then.
lines.literal: good plan. I wonder only if I have-time home before seven, since I shall call mom then.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Inga problem. Båtarna går ofta, så vi kan åka hem när du vill.
lines.id: No problem. The boats run often, so we can go home whenever you like.
lines.literal: no problems. boats-the go often, so we can go home when you want.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Då säger vi så. Jag skickar ett sms när jag har kollat tiderna.
lines.id: Let's say that, then. I'll text you when I've checked the times.
lines.literal: then say we so. I send an SMS when I have checked times-the.

lines.speaker: Oskar:
lines.text: Toppen. Hörs!
lines.id: Great. Talk soon!
lines.literal: top-the. hear-each-other!

notes: **Tänkte jag att vi kunde…** — a very Swedish way to suggest something gently: "I was thinking we could…". The past tense (*tänkte*, *kunde*) makes it softer than *Vi kan åka ut*. Notice the verb-first order again: the *om*-clause filled the first slot.

**Hur man tar sig dit** — *ta sig* + direction means "to get (somewhere)": *Hur tar jag mig till stationen?* It's reflexive, so the pronoun changes: *jag tar **mig***, *man tar **sig***. And *hur man tar sig dit* is an indirect question: subject before verb.

**Skärgården** (**HWEHR-goh-den**) — the archipelago. Both Stockholm and Göteborg have one right on their doorstep. Göteborg's southern islands, like Styrsö, have no cars, and the boats are part of ordinary public transport — so yes, the monthly pass (*månadskortet*) is valid.
**Det ingår** — *ingå* (**IN-goh**) means "to be included": *Frukost ingår* (breakfast is included). Stress falls on the first part: this is one of the fused particle verbs you'll meet in Unit 7.

**Vad gör vi om det regnar?** — notice that the main clause comes first here, so there's no inversion problem at all. When the *om*-clause comes first, the main clause starts with the verb: *Om det regnar, **går vi**…*
**Hörs!** (**hösh**) — "Talk soon!", from *höras* (hear each other), the phone and text cousin of *Vi ses!*. *Tjena!* (**SHEH-nah**) is a casual "Hi!", and *Toppen!* means "Great!".

grammars.title: Indirect questions and att-clauses
body: When a question is tucked inside a longer sentence ("Do you know **when the boats leave**?"), it becomes a subordinate clause. Two things happen: the subject comes **before** the verb, and sentence adverbs go **in front of** the verb (BIFF). English does the first one too — "when the boats leave", not "when do the boats leave".

head: Direct question
Indirect question
rows: Vet du **om kortet gäller** på båten?
Jag vet inte **hur man tar sig dit**.
Jag undrar **om jag hinner** hem innan sju.

after: **Yes/no questions** become *om*-clauses ("whether, if"); **question-word questions** keep their question word: *när, var, hur, varför, vad, vem, vilken*.
When the question word itself is the **subject**, Swedish adds *som*: *Vem ringde?* → *Jag vet inte **vem som** ringde.* Unit 11 deals with *vad som* and *det som* in detail.

**Att** is often dropped after *tror, tycker, säger, hoppas, vet*: *Jag tror (att) hon kommer.* With a negation, Swedes prefer to negate the main verb, just like English: *Jag **tror inte** att hon kommer* (I don't think she's coming).

blocks.text: Long Swedish sentences are not harder than short ones — they are short ones stacked together. The trick is to know, at every moment, whether you are in a **main clause** (verb second, *inte* after the verb) or a **subordinate clause** (subject–adverb–verb). The linking word tells you.

head: Linking word
Meaning
Example
rows: Vi åker ut **även om** det blåser.
Hon kom **trots att** hon var sjuk.
Han gick **utan att** säga hej då.
Vi tog båten **i stället för att** åka buss.
Skicka dem nu **så att** han hinner läsa.

blocks.title: Stacking a sentence in four steps
items: **1. Main clause:** *Jag skickar skisserna.*
**2. Add time:** *Jag skickar skisserna **innan Mattias går på mötet**.*
**3. Add a condition in front:** ***Om Karin vill**, skickar jag skisserna innan Mattias går på mötet.*
**4. Add an indirect question:** *Om Karin vill, skickar jag skisserna innan Mattias går på mötet, **men jag vet inte när mötet börjar**.*
Read the final sentence aloud and point at each verb: is it second (main clause) or after the subject (subordinate clause)?

blocks.text: For Göteborgers, an island day means smooth pink granite rocks (*klippor*) that warm up in the sun, a swim from the rocks even when the water is 17 degrees, a coffee from a thermos, and the boat home in the evening light. Swedes check the forecast obsessively: *Vad säger prognosen?* is a normal question on a Friday.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 3
items: Put a sentence adverb into five subordinate clauses: *…eftersom kunden **aldrig** har sett…*, *…om båten **kanske** är sen…*, *…att han **inte** hinner…*
Then move each subordinate clause to the front and check the verb: ***Eftersom kunden aldrig har sett dem, behöver** vi förklara dem.*
Front an object in the main clause, too, for a final challenge: *Skisserna skickar jag innan han går.*

exercises.prompt: Move the subordinate clause to the front. Watch the verb in the main clause.
items: Vi kan ses imorgon om du vill.

Vi går på museum om det regnar.
Han hade redan gått innan jag kom.
